itemListElement.text: In a small bowl, stir together water, honey, and salt then sprinkle the top with 1/2 tsp yeast and let sit 5 minutes then stir.
itemListElement.name: In a small bowl, stir together water, honey, and salt then sprinkle the top with 1/2 tsp yeast and let sit 5 minutes then stir.

itemListElement.text: Measure 3 1/3 cups flour in a large mixing bowl and make a well in the center. Pour yeast mixture into the center then stir with a firm spatula until the dough comes together. Knead by hand 2 minutes (dough will be sticky). Cover the bowl with plastic wrap and let rise at room temperature 4-5 hours or until doubled in size.
itemListElement.name: Measure 3 1/3 cups flour in a large mixing bowl and make a well in the center. Pour yeast mixture into the center then stir with a firm spatula until the dough comes together. Knead by hand 2 minutes (dough will be sticky). Cover the bowl with plastic wrap and let rise at room temperature 4-5 hours or until doubled in size.

itemListElement.text: Transfer dough to a floured surface, turn to coat lightly in flour so it isn’t sticky then divide in half. Fold each piece of dough in half 8 times, gently pulling the sides over the center like closing a book, turning the dough each time and repeating for 8 folds. Form a ball in your hands and transfer each piece of dough to a lightly oiled bowl seam-side-down, cover and refrigerate overnight (18 hours) or up to 1 week.

recipeInstructions.name: How to Form a Pizza Crust:

itemListElement.text: PREP: Remove the dough 1 hour before using to let it relax and come to room temperature. Before forming the pizza crust, fully preheat your oven so pizza can be baked right away. Place a pizza stone or inverted baking sheet onto the center rack of the oven and preheat to 550˚F. Also, lightly flour a pizza peel and prep toppings.
itemListElement.name: PREP: Remove the dough 1 hour before using to let it relax and come to room temperature. Before forming the pizza crust, fully preheat your oven so pizza can be baked right away. Place a pizza stone or inverted baking sheet onto the center rack of the oven and preheat to 550˚F. Also, lightly flour a pizza peel and prep toppings.

itemListElement.text: When dough is about room temperature and oven is preheated, transfer 1 piece of dough to a floured surface, turning to lightly coat in flour. Pat the center of the dough gently with fingertips. DO NOT pop any bubbles present.
itemListElement.name: When dough is about room temperature and oven is preheated, transfer 1 piece of dough to a floured surface, turning to lightly coat in flour. Pat the center of the dough gently with fingertips. DO NOT pop any bubbles present.

itemListElement.text: Lift the dough over both knuckles and roll your knuckles under the center of the dough, working outward as you rotate the dough along your knuckles and leaving a thicker crust at the edge. Continue working the dough until a 10-12” pizza has formed. It will shrink slightly so make it a little bigger than you think. Place the dough down on a lightly floured pizza peel. Give the pizza peel a little shake to make sure the pizza slides over it and is not sticking.
itemListElement.name: Lift the dough over both knuckles and roll your knuckles under the center of the dough, working outward as you rotate the dough along your knuckles and leaving a thicker crust at the edge. Continue working the dough until a 10-12” pizza has formed. It will shrink slightly so make it a little bigger than you think. Place the dough down on a lightly floured pizza peel. Give the pizza peel a little shake to make sure the pizza slides over it and is not sticking.

itemListElement.text: Spread on desired pizza sauce and toppings. Give the pizza another jolt to make sure it slides on the pizza peel (you don’t want it to stick while transferring it into the oven). Slide pizza onto the preheated pizza stone and bake at 550˚F for 8-10 minutes or until crust is golden brown and some of the larger bubbles on the crust are lightly scorched to ensure a crisp crust.

review.reviewBody: Prior to trying your pizza dough recipe, I tried many other recipes, which were good, but not great.  My first time using this recipe was a success.  It produced a crust that was crisp and chewy.  I have been using this recipe for quite some time now and I have perfected my abilities to constantly produce a nice thin crispy bottom crust with edges that are puffed, airy, and with the perfect amount of chew.  I found the video to be very helpful.  Natasha, thank you for a great recipe that allowed a pizza making novice like me to succeed!

Thank you!  This is now my go-to pizza dough recipe after trying several others.  It was easy, relatively quick and had good flavor.  The KEY reason I love it, though, is that the dough stayed stretched out when I put it onto the peel, it didn't shrink back.  This has been a challenge with other doughs (even at room temp. they stretch unevenly and then shrink back to half the size).  This one didn't, so I could get the round, thin, stretched-out shape like a professional!  Ha ha! 

I only had rapid-rise instant yeast so I used it as per the recipe.  Also I used rice flour on the pizza peel, a recommendation I got in Naples, Italy (less likely to burn, they said).  We have an outdoor pizza oven. 

I assume this dough will freeze - we have done that successfully with other pizza doughs.  Just allow enough time for it to thaw on the counter and come to room temp.

We love this pie.  Today we harvested the first tomatoes of this season.  Our basil is lush and fragrant.  So I did what any logical person would do; made Pizza Margherita.  It rocks Margherita style.

Made this true to recipe, only added some seasoning (Italian, garlic) to the flour before adding wet ingredients. Let it rise for ~3 days in the fridge before using it. It turned out AMAZING. Best homemade pizza dough I’ve tried.
